# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +307
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T15:05:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The re-arm self-heal design is sound and the script/workflow changes are well-reasoned, but the new `gh-1561` dart test has an **inverted tagger-date assertion** — I ran `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart` locally (dart works on this host) and it fails 43/44 with exactly the tagger-date check (actual 119 min vs expected <10). The assertion as written only passes when the tag was NOT re-cut. Two workflow issues accompany it: the App-token mint omits the `permissions: contents:write` least-privilege constraint that ci.yml:3848 carries per the gh-1172 round-2 review, and the "fails over to the manual-fix alarm without the secret" claim does not hold — a missing `RELEASE_APP_ID` fails the mint step and kills the job before the verify step ever runs.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 `test/release_flow_race_test.dart:809` — inverted freshness assertion; the test-core gate reddens (reproduced locally).
- ⚠️ `daily-publish.yml:545` — App token minted with the installation's full grants instead of explicit `permissions: contents:write`.
- ⚠️ `daily-publish.yml:542` — missing-secret failover is a hard step failure, not the script's manual-fix alarm.

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix the tagger-date assertion to require the FRESH date (compare `actual` to `now`, or `greaterThan(100)` against `seeded`).
2. Add `permissions: contents: write` to the mint step (match ci.yml).
3. Make the mint step tolerant of missing secrets (`continue-on-error: true`) so the script's existing empty-`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN` path actually runs.
4. Optional: bounded poll for run registration after the re-arm (a single 10s re-read will frequently alarm despite a successful re-arm).

---

### Thread 9

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):

fixes incoming — blocker + both importants + the re-arm-flow suggestions in one push; replies per thread as each lands.

### Thread 11

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-12):
Drill correction (red run 38245365741, zero jobs): the rework's 'least-privilege' was implemented as a step-level `permissions: contents: none` block — GitHub Actions has no permissions key on STEPS, so the whole workflow failed validation. Dropped on 9f7f8685c; least-privilege is enforced at JOB level (contents: read + actions: write), which the mint step inherits — job-level permissions unchanged from main. Lesson recorded: ruby-YAML parse checks validate syntax, not the Actions schema.

### Thread 12

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-12):
Drill closure (push-ghost chain, 3 zero-job runs 38245365741 → 38245715756 → 38246659028): root cause was NEVER the step-level `permissions` key alone — it was the `secrets.*` context in the mint step's `if:` expression, which GitHub's workflow validator rejects on the ref's file copy (the file has no push trigger, so each push only created a validator verdict run). Fixed on ac314b957 by mirroring the validator-proven ci.yml release-job mint shape exactly: no `if:`, `continue-on-error: true` (unconfigured App → swallowed failure → empty token → script's manual-re-push alarm), and the least-privilege ceiling as the action's `permissions: contents:write` WITH input (same as ci.yml:3848). Validator proof: the ac314b957 push — which touches the workflow file — created NO daily-publish run at all, while every prior push did. Legacy lesson recorded: ruby-YAML parse checks syntax, not the Actions expression schema; the review lesson is the ci.yml-precedent-mirror rule.

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):

🚨 **BLOCKING: Inverted assertion — the test gate fails (reproduced locally)**

I ran `dart test test/release_flow_race_test.dart` on this host (the dart VM works here despite the PR disclosure). Result: **43 passed, 1 failed**:

```
❌ gh-1561 — re-arm registers the fresh push run -> the leg continues with it (neutral skip)
Expected: a value less than <10>
  Actual: <119>
  test/release_flow_race_test.dart 807:9
```

The matcher is inverted. The seeded tag is backdated 2h, so:

- If the re-arm **worked** (the tag was re-cut with a fresh tagger date): `actual ≈ now`, and `actual.difference(seeded) ≈ 120 min` → the assertion **fails**.
- If the re-arm **did not happen** (tagger date still the backdated one): `actual ≈ seeded` → difference `≈ 0` → the assertion passes.

So this check verifies the opposite of its stated intent — it only passes when the tag was NOT re-armed. In the same test the earlier assertions (`contains('re-armed')`, `inFlight`, `run_url`) all pass, confirming the re-arm genuinely happened and the date check as written cannot succeed. This reddens the `test-core` CI stage.

Fix — assert the re-cut tag is fresh relative to now:

```dart
expect(
  DateTime.now().toUtc().difference(actual).inMinutes,
  lessThan(10),
  reason: 'the re-arm re-cut the tag at the SAME commit (fresh date)',
);
```

(or keep the `seeded` comparison but require `greaterThan(100)`). This also invalidates the "27/27 assertions pass" claim in the PR description's local-gate section — worth a re-run of the hand-driven replica after the fix.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Missing least-privilege `permissions` on the App-token mint**

ci.yml's release job mints this exact token with an explicit permission ceiling (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3848`):

```yaml

# the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
```

`actions/create-github-app-token` v3 defaults differently: when `permissions` is omitted, the minted token receives **all permissions granted to the App installation** — not just what the re-arm needs. The re-arm only force-pushes one tag ref, so `contents:write` is the whole requirement, and the repo's own precedent (a review requirement from gh-1172 round 2) demands the explicit ceiling. A broader-than-necessary write token should not sit in the environment of a step whose script fetches remote data.

Match the established pattern:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permissions: contents:write
```

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: The missing-secret failover claim does not hold at the workflow level**

The PR description states: "without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm." But if `RELEASE_APP_ID` / `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are unset or misconfigured (forks, a rotation gap, a replay in another repo), this step fails hard — `actions/create-github-app-token` errors with "Input required and not supplied: app-id" — and the **job dies here**, before the `Verify pub.dev` step ever runs. The script's graceful empty-`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN` path (the actual failover, `rearm_tag` returning 1 → unchanged manual alarm) is never reached; instead the leg reports an unclassified step failure with no `status` output.

The script side of the failover is already written and tested — the workflow just never lets it execute. Make the mint non-fatal:

```yaml

        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true # missing secrets -> token empty -> the script's manual-fix alarm
        with:
          ...
```

`steps.app-token.outputs.token` is then empty on failure, `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN` is empty, and the tested failover path …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +307
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T15:05:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi
  if [ "$a" -lt 1 ]; then a=1; fi
  echo "$a"
}

# gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG — the committed
# pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder. The `pubspec=` output key name is
# kept (daily-publish report consumers read it), its value is the tag
# version. No remote tags → nothing has ever been released → up-to-date.
latest_remote_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v*' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -v '\^' | awk '{print $2}' | sed 's|refs/tags/||' \
  | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1 || true)
pubspec="${latest_remote_tag#v}"
emit "pubspec=$pubspec"
emit "published=" # re-exported below after query

if grep -q '^publish_to: *none' pubspec.yaml; then
  emit "status=private"
  echo "::notice::pubspec declares publish_to: none — package is private, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

if [ -z "$pubspec" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"
  echo "::notice::no vX.Y.Z tags on the remote — nothing has been released yet, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0
fi

# pub.dev API reads lag minutes behind a fresh publish (CDN replicas) — a
# single stale read must not send us into recovery. Three spaced reads, take
# the newest by version. Fails (non-zero) when the API is unreachable —
# callers decide whether that is fatal.
read_published_version() {
  local acc="" v attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version')
    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
  done
  printf '%s' "$acc"
}

published=""
published=$(read_published_version)
emit "published=$published"
echo "pubspec=$pubspec published=$published"
newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)
if [ "$newest" = "$published" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"
  echo "::notice::pub.dev already serves $published"
  exit 0
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
  echo "::error::$tag has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered ($1). Manual fix: re-push the tag (git push origin $tag --force) or run ci.yml on the tag ref."
  exit 1
}

# gh-1561: re-arm a tag whose push twin never fired. Recreate the annotated
# tag object on the SAME commit (new tagger date -> new oid -> the ref
# update fires a real tag-push event, which a same-oid push never would)
# and force-push it with the App token. The commit is read from the remote
# tag and pushed back unchanged — the re-arm never moves what the tag
# points at, only re-announces it. RELEASE_APP_PUSH_URL overrides the push
# destination (test seam; production derives it from RELEASE_APP_TOKEN).
rearm_tag() {
  if [ -z "${RELEASE_APP_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    echo "RELEASE_APP_TOKEN not set — cannot re-arm $tag automatically (a GITHUB_TOKEN push cannot cascade); manual re-push required"
    return 1
  fi
  local commit
  commit=$(git rev-parse "$tag^{commit}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  git -c user.name='fa-release-bot[bot]' \
      -c user.email='fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
      tag -a -f "$tag" "$commit" \
      -m "Release $tag (re-armed: the original push never triggered a ci.yml run)" \
    || return 1
  git push --force \
    "${RELEASE_APP_PUSH_URL:-https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" \
    "refs/tags/$tag" \
    || return 1
  echo "re-armed $tag at ${commit:0:12} (same commit, fresh tag object) — waiting for the fresh push run to register"
}

# The tag's ci.yml runs. Only PUSH-event runs can publish in THIS repo: the
# publish job's `if` requires `github.event_name == 'push'` (#1368 — the
# release arm is gone; pub.dev OIDC accepts push/workflow_dispatch tokens,
# but a rerun keeps the original event, so re-running a dispatch twin would
# still not publish). Classification and recovery use a push run, never the
# release twin. One list read, filtered locally.
fetch_runs() {
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --limit 20 \
    --json databaseId,status,conclusion,event
}
push_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c 'map(select(.event == "push")) | .[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}
any_run_of() { # $1 = runs JSON array
  jq -c '.[0] // empty' <<<"$1"
}

# Tag presence + age. creatordate = the annotated tag's tagger date (the
# moment auto_release.sh cut it); a lightweight tag falls back to its commit
# date. The timestamp is sampled per call — after a wait a just-pushed tag
# must not read as a negative age (#1370 review).
read_tag_age() {
  if git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "refs/tags/$tag:refs/tags/$tag"
    echo "$(( $(date +%s) - $(git for-each-ref "refs/tags/$tag" --format='%(creatordate:unix)') ))"
  fi
}
tag_age=$(read_tag_age)

# gh-1522: the version IS the latest remote tag, so the tag exists by
# construction — a missing tag here means it was deleted between the
# ls-remote above and this read (or a transient fetch failure). That is
# unobserved, not an alarm: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
if [ -z "$tag_age" ]; then
  in_flight "$tag is not visible (deleted mid-run or a transient fetch failure)"
fi

runs_json=$(fetch_runs)
tag_run=$(push_run_of "$runs_json")
if [ -z "$tag_run" ]; then
  # AC1 — the 2026-10-03 #1189 false positive: between `git push <tag>` and
  # the tag's ci.yml run becoming visible there is a seconds-to-minutes
  # window (tag 05:32, verify 05:35 read «no run», the healthy run
  # completed 05:37). auto_release.sh cuts the GitHub Release concurrently
  # with the tag push, so the RELEASE twin can register while the push twin
  # has not — the grace window governs before ANY «never triggered» verdict
  # (#1370 review r2): a young tag is release-in-flight, full stop.
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt "$grace" ]; then
    in_flight "$tag exists (${tag_age}s old < ${grace}s grace) but its push ci.yml run is not visible yet"
  fi
  # Review thread 2 (E4 residual): a freshly re-pushed tag takes seconds to
  # register in the API — an operator re-pushing while this leg sits between
  # its `git ls-remote` and the read above must not trip «never triggered»
  # once. One spaced re-read; alarm only if it is empty too.
  sleep "$read_sleep"
  runs_json=$(fetch_runs)
  tag_run=$(push_run_of "$runs_json")

    echo "::notice::$tag's ci run registered between the reads — continuing with it"
  fi

    reason="only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only"

  # ci.yml's release job LANDED (tag + release both registered) but its
  # push twin never fired, and a release-API tag (server-side creation)
  # never fires a push event at all. Re-arm before alarming (see above).
  if rearm_tag; then
    # A fresh tag-push run takes tens of seconds to register — one 10s
    # re-read would alarm (and self-file a «re-push the tag» issue!)
    # exactly when the self-heal worked. Bounded registration wait instead;
    # past it the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never failed (#1370 doctrine):
    # neutral skip — the next daily re-verifies the run the re-arm left
    # behind (E4: a completed fresh run verifies normally).
    registration_reads="${REARM_REG_READS:-6}"
    attempt=1
    while [ "$attempt" -le "$registration_reads" ]; do
      sleep "$read_sleep"
      runs_json=$(fetch_runs)
      tag_run=$(push_run_of "$runs_json")
      [ -n "$tag_run" ] && break
      attempt=$(( attempt + 1 ))
    done
    if [ -n "$tag_run" ]; then
      echo "::notice::$tag re-armed — its fresh push ci.yml run registered, continuing with it"
    fi
    if [ -z "$tag_run" ]; then
      in_flight "$tag was re-armed by this leg but its fresh push run has not registered yet — outcome unobserved, the next daily re-verifies"
    fi
  fi
  if [ -z "$tag_run" ]; then
    # AC2 — no push run (e.g. a GITHUB_TOKEN push cannot cascade) and the
    # re-arm could not run or push (no token, push rejected): the manual
    # alarm, text unchanged.
    never_triggered "$reason"

fi

  # state (bounded) before classifying, instead of skipping on the first
  # pending read. Once the budget lapses the outcome is still unobserved —
  # stay neutral (runner starvation can hold a queued run for hours; the
  # next daily re-verifies).

    in_flight "the $tag push run succeeded but the pub.dev API is unreachable — outcome unobserved, the next daily re-verifies"

  echo "::error::tag run for $tag succeeded but pub.dev still serves $fresh (was $published) — publish did not upload. Manual publish needed (see issue)."

# An unreadable conclusion (transient API failure) may hide a successful
# run — `rerun --failed` on it fails to start; fail loud, never fall off
# set -e mid-recovery (#1370 review).
if ! gh run rerun "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --failed 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::could not start the rerun of the $tag publish run ($run_id, concluded $conclusion) — manual recovery needed: https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  exit 1
fi
sleep "$poll_sleep"
# Bounded watch — the leg's 60m ceiling must survive appear-wait + rerun +
# post-verify (thread: budget arithmetic); `timeout` is absent on some
# dev hosts (macOS/BSD), fall back to the unbounded watch there.
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  timeout 900 gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
else
  gh run watch "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --exit-status --interval 60 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rstatus=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
conclusion=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json conclusion --jq .conclusion 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)

  # executing — outcome unobserved: neutral skip, the next daily re-verifies.
  in_flight "rerun of the $tag publish run is $rstatus — outcome unobserved, not failed"
fi
if [ "$conclusion" != "success" ]; then

fi

  sleep "$poll_sleep"

  exit 1
fi
emit "status=recovered"
echo "::notice::recovered — re-ran the $tag publish run, pub.dev now serves $pubspec"

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +307
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T15:05:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window

#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for

#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version

# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the

#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is

# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.

set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi

published=$(read_published_version)
emit "published=$published"
echo "pubspec=$pubspec published=$published"
newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)
if [ "$newest" = "$published" ]; then
  emit "status=up-to-date"

  exit 0
fi

# Behind: classify the tag's publish state before reaching for recovery.
tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm
  emit "status=release-in-flight"
  echo "::notice::skipped: release in flight — $1; the next scheduled daily re-verifies."
  exit 0
}

never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight

      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). No inputs to disambiguate on
          # (newest-in-tight-window fallback), watch bounded at 60m =

            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --budget-seconds 3600 \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent exactly (ci.yml release
      # job, the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change. The
      # least-privilege ceiling rides the action's `permissions` input
      # (contents:write covers the tag re-push), identical to the precedent.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permissions: contents:write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile

```

(or keep the `seeded` comparison but require `greaterThan(100)`). This also invalidates the "27/27 assertions pass" claim in the PR description's local-gate section — worth a re-run of the hand-driven replica after the fix.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Missing least-privilege `permissions` on the App-token mint**

ci.yml's release job mints this exact token with an explicit permission ceiling (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3848`):

```yaml
permissions: contents:write
# Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
# the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
```

`actions/create-github-app-token` v3 defaults differently: when `permissions` is omitted, the minted token receives **all permissions granted to the App installation** — not just what the re-arm needs. The re-arm only force-pushes one tag ref, so `contents:write` is the whole requirement, and the repo's own precedent (a review requirement from gh-1172 round 2) demands the explicit ceiling. A broader-than-necessary write token should not sit in the environment of a step whose script fetches remote data.

Match the established pattern:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permissions: contents:write
```

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-12):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: The missing-secret failover claim does not hold at the workflow level**

The PR description states: "without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm." But if `RELEASE_APP_ID` / `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` are unset or misconfigured (forks, a rotation gap, a replay in another repo), this step fails hard — `actions/create-github-app-token` errors with "Input required and not supplied: app-id" — and the **job dies here**, before the `Verify pub.dev` step ever runs. The script's graceful empty-`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN` path (the actual failover, `rearm_tag` returning 1 → unchanged manual alarm) is never reached; instead the leg reports an unclassified step failure with no `status` output.

The script side of the failover is already written and tested — the workflow just never lets it execute. Make the mint non-fatal:

```yaml

        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true # missing secrets -> token empty -> the script's manual-fix alarm
        with:
          ...
```

`steps.app-token.outputs.token` is then empty on failure, `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN` is empty, and the tested failover path …

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner
#                           starvation may hold a queued run for hours
#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +307
- **Deletions**: -13
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T15:05:52Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

The full diff is available in the checked-out PR branch. Use `git diff` or CodeGraph for focused source navigation instead of relying only on this file.

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml b/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml
index e4d1a76ad..90388c473 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml
@@ -535,11 +535,37 @@ jobs:
           echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
           exit 1
 
+      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
+      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
+      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
+      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
+      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
+      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent exactly (ci.yml release
+      # job, the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
+      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
+      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
+      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
+      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change. The
+      # least-privilege ceiling rides the action's `permissions` input
+      # (contents:write covers the tag re-push), identical to the precedent.
+      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
+        id: app-token
+        continue-on-error: true
+        with:
+          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
+          permissions: contents:write
+
       - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
         id: check
         # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
         # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
         # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
+        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
+        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
+        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
+        env:
+          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
         run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh
 
   # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
diff --git a/scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh b/scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh
index fa5f32bf6..b3f7e8103 100755
--- a/scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh
+++ b/scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh
@@ -47,6 +47,15 @@
 # has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
 # run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
 #
+# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
+# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
+# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
+# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
+# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
+# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
+# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
+# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
+#
 # E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
 set -euo pipefail
 
@@ -107,14 +116,21 @@ fi
 
 # pub.dev API reads lag minutes behind a fresh publish (CDN replicas) — a
 # single stale read must not send us into recovery. Three spaced reads, take
-# the newest by version.
+# the newest by version. Fails (non-zero) when the API is unreachable —
+# callers decide whether that is fatal.
+read_published_version() {
+  local acc="" v attempt
+  for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+    v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
+      https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version')
+    acc=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$acc" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
+    [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
+  done
+  printf '%s' "$acc"
+}
+
 published=""
-for attempt in 1 2 3; do
-  v=$(curl -fsS --retry 3 \
-    https://pub.dev/api/packages/flutter_agent_harness | jq -r '.latest.version')
-  published=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$published" "$v" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -V | tail -1)
-  [ "$attempt" = 3 ] || sleep "$read_sleep"
-done
+published=$(read_published_version)
 emit "published=$published"
 echo "pubspec=$pubspec published=$published"
 newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)
@@ -138,6 +154,32 @@ never_triggered() { # $1 = which state — nothing publishable is in flight
   exit 1
 }
 
+# gh-1561: re-arm a tag whose push twin never fired. Recreate the annotated
+# tag object on the SAME commit (new tagger date -> new oid -> the ref
+# update fires a real tag-push event, which a same-oid push never would)
+# and force-push it with the App token. The commit is read from the remote
+# tag and pushed back unchanged — the re-arm never moves what the tag
+# points at, only re-announces it. RELEASE_APP_PUSH_URL overrides the push
+# destination (test seam; production derives it from RELEASE_APP_TOKEN).
+rearm_tag() {
+  if [ -z "${RELEASE_APP_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
+    echo "RELEASE_APP_TOKEN not set — cannot re-arm $tag automatically (a GITHUB_TOKEN push cannot cascade); manual re-push required"
+    return 1
+  fi
+  local commit
+  commit=$(git rev-parse "$tag^{commit}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+  git -c user.name='fa-release-bot[bot]' \
+      -c user.email='fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
+      tag -a -f "$tag" "$commit" \
+      -m "Release $tag (re-armed: the original push never triggered a ci.yml run)" \
+    || return 1
+  git push --force \
+    "${RELEASE_APP_PUSH_URL:-https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${repo}.git}" \
+    "refs/tags/$tag" \
+    || return 1

- ⚠️ `daily-publish.yml:545` — App token minted with the installation's full grants instead of explicit `permissions: contents:write`.
- ⚠️ `daily-publish.yml:542` — missing-secret failover is a hard step failure, not the script's manual-fix alarm.

1. Fix the tagger-date assertion to require the FRESH date (compare `actual` to `now`, or `greaterThan(100)` against `seeded`).

The matcher is inverted. The seeded tag is backdated 2h, so:

  lessThan(10),

);

        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permissions: contents:write
